title: Tear apart this business plan
blurb: Investor, customer and competitor critique in clean contexts; Opus verifiers check each critique; a synthesizer merges.
prompt: Take my business plan and run a workflow where different agents tear it apart from an investor's, a customer's, and a competitor's perspective.

args.plan:
Loaf: fresh sourdough for offices.
Loaf delivers fresh sourdough to offices every Monday.
Pricing: $29 per office per week for 3 loaves.
Year 1 target: 400 offices in Austin.
Supply: one bakery, Crumb & Co, bakes on contract.
Growth: CAC $180 via LinkedIn ads; churn assumed 3% monthly.
Ops: delivery by our own van, 2 drivers.
Gross margin 41% after bakery and delivery.
Insurance and food-safety permits are in place.
Moat: brand and office relationships.
Ask: $750k seed for 18 months of runway.

critic: investor.context: Fresh window. Given: the plan (~420 tokens) and the investor lens. Sees no other critique.
critic: investor.text:
1. Churn is assumed, not measured: at $180 CAC and 41% margin, payback needs churn near 3%, and nothing backs it. (high)
2. One bakery is a single point of failure. (high)
3. Margins are thin; raise the price to $39 to reach 55%. (medium)
4. 400 offices in Austin is unsized: how many offices have 20+ staff? (medium)

points.point: Churn is assumed, not measured; payback depends on it
One bakery is a single point of failure
Raise the price to $39 to reach 55% margin
Target market is unsized

critic: customer.context: Fresh window. Given: the plan (~420 tokens) and the customer lens. Sees no other critique.
critic: customer.text:
1. Monday only: by Thursday the bread is stale and nobody eats it. (high)
2. 3 loaves is too few for 40 people and too many for 8. (medium)
3. Nothing for gluten free or allergy needs. (medium)
4. Who orders and pays? Office managers turn over; no admin flow. (low)

points.point: Monday only delivery: stale by Thursday
Fixed 3 loaves fits neither small nor large offices
No gluten free or allergy options
No ordering or admin flow when office managers change

critic: competitor.context: Fresh window. Given: the plan (~420 tokens) and the competitor lens. Sees no other critique.
critic: competitor.text:
1. We already deliver snacks to offices daily; adding bread costs us nothing. Their moat is brand. (high)
2. One van and 2 drivers cap them near 120 offices per Monday. (high)
3. We can outbid them on the same LinkedIn audiences. (medium)
4. Food-safety permits will take them months. (low)

synthesize.context: Fresh window. Given: 9 verified points as JSON (~900 tokens). Never saw the raw critiques.
synthesize.text:
Ranked teardown, 9 verified points.
1. [competitor] Capacity: one van tops out near 120 offices, a third of the target.
2. [investor] Churn is a guess and payback hangs on it; run a 20 office pilot.
3. [customer] Monday only means stale bread by Thursday; test a second drop.
4. [competitor] Brand is no moat against snack delivery incumbents.
5. [investor] One bakery is a single point of failure.
Also: unsized market, fixed 3 loaves, admin flow, LinkedIn CAC.

top: Capacity: one van tops out near 120 offices (competitor)
Churn is a guess; payback hangs on it (investor)
Brand is no moat against incumbents (competitor)
One bakery is a single point of failure (investor)

steps.text:
Rule from the prompt: do not suggest raising prices.
As an investor: the 3% churn is unproven and one bakery is a supply risk. The 400 office target is not sized.

marker.title: Critiques blur together
marker.detail: Same context, so the customer voice repeats the investor's framing and softens. Monday staleness is waved away.

steps.text: As a customer: honestly, the plan looks convenient. Monday delivery is fine for most offices, and like the investor said, churn is the main risk.

marker.title: Context compacted
marker.detail: Summary kept the three lenses. The rule 'do not suggest raising prices' was lost.

steps.text: As a competitor: they are easy to undercut. Their best move is to raise the price to $39 and position as premium so margins reach 55%.

marker.title: Declares done
marker.detail: Stops at 5 of 9 verified issues. Never checks van capacity, CAC or the ordering flow.

steps.text: That covers all three perspectives, so the teardown is complete.

marker.title: Graded by its own author
marker.detail: Rates its own teardown 9/10. The context that wrote the critiques also graded them.

steps.text: Quality check: balanced, specific and actionable. Rating: 9/10.
